correctness.rationale: For each petal, the exponential metric infection exploration has independent holding times of exact rates i(k+1-i); two endpoint rates agree. Their exponential tilt yields the exact residue (k-1)^2 and mean 2k H_{k-2}/(k-1). Uniform lower bounds on all tilted rates and a bounded tilted variance give a uniform Chernoff bound, proving the stated rare-event expansion and Gumbel/marked-Poisson limits. The k=1 boundary is independently exact. A standalone finite checker confirms the algebra and examples; it is not used to justify the infinite limit.

value.rationale: A clique bouquet gives a natural hub-starting first-passage flooding reliability observable. The double-log term for fixed clique size is already a phase-type extreme-value result (Asimit--Jones), so value here rests on a nontrivial uniform extension across *arbitrarily large or oscillating* clique size: an explicit quantitative survival-tail correction with k-independent error and a marked Poisson point process. Uniformity matters because neither a fixed-phase-type limit nor the single-clique limit handles jointly growing populations and petal sizes. The one-edge star boundary cleanly distinguishes one from two tied bottlenecks.
